span.p:
BEFORE the fix:
always 200,
regardless of healthy

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
AFTER the fix:
JSONResponse(status_code=
200 if healthy else 503)

span.p: No (1st failure)

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
real gap found:
HALF_OPEN state

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Kubernetes kubelet:
every readinessProbe.periodSeconds (3s),
httpGet /health on each pod

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
app.py : health()
snapshot = breaker.snapshot()

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: healthy = snapshot.state != OPEN

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
the REAL bug found here:
what HTTP status does
the response carry?

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
kubelet sees HTTP 200
→ ALWAYS marks pod Ready
→ probe is USELESS

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
kubelet actually distinguishes
healthy vs. unhealthy pods

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
probe result:
200 or 503?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
pod stays in Ready condition
→ stays in Service's
Endpoints list

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
failureThreshold (2)
consecutive 503s reached?

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
pod still marked Ready
(tolerating one blip)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
kubelet marks pod NotReady
→ Kubernetes Endpoint controller
REMOVES pod IP from
Service's Endpoints

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Service no longer routes
any traffic to this pod
— verified live by stopping
Ollama and watching this happen

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
separately, every livenessProbe.periodSeconds
(10s), SAME /health endpoint checked

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
failureThreshold (5)
consecutive failures?
— deliberately MORE tolerant
than readiness

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: pod keeps running

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
kubelet RESTARTS the container
— only for a truly stuck process,
not a transient downstream outage

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
breaker auto-transitions
OPEN → HALF_OPEN after cooldown,
and HALF_OPEN counts as 'healthy'
— but /health NEVER actively
pings Ollama itself

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
with NO real /generate traffic,
pod can read 'ready=true' again
even though Ollama is STILL DOWN
— documented, not silently fixed
